adds.rationale: First pure-play humanoid robotics/physical-AI ETF gives the watchlist direct exposure to the profile's #2 next-wave priority, which was previously only proxied indirectly through Teradyne's small Universal Robots segment; September's mega Series C into Figure AI confirms the wave is now in a capital-buildup phase.

news_evidence.summary: KraneShares Global Humanoid Robotics and Physical AI Index ETF (KOID), the first U.S.-listed humanoid-robotics ETF, began trading on Nasdaq, tracking ~50-58 companies across humanoid manufacturing, actuation, sensing, semiconductors and critical materials
Humanoid robotics startup Figure AI raised over $1B in Series C funding at a $39B post-money valuation, backed by Nvidia, Brookfield, Intel Capital, Salesforce and Qualcomm Ventures

removes.rationale: Teradyne's Q2 2025 print showed core semiconductor-test revenue declining year-over-year even as it beat depressed guidance, and its Robotics segment (Universal Robots) is only ~11% of quarterly sales, so it is a weak, indirect proxy for the robotics wave and largely redundant AI-capex exposure already carried by MSFT/GOOGL/NVDA; swapping it for a direct robotics vehicle sharpens thematic coverage without adding a ticker.

news_evidence.summary: Teradyne reported Q2 2025 revenue of $652M ($492M Semiconductor Test, $75M Robotics, $85M Product Test); beat the midpoint of guidance but revenue was down year-over-year

rationale_overall: Every current holding still showed live, in-quarter buildup evidence (GOOGL and MSFT posted accelerating cloud/Azure growth on July 23 and July 30; NVDA's Aug 27 print and $60B buyback confirmed AI capex is still surging; OKLO landed DOE Reactor Pilot Program and Fuel Recycling Facility wins plus an Aurora groundbreaking; ASTS advanced FCC SCSA authorization and BlueBird 6 assembly in early September; RKLB signed a 10-launch Synspective deal in September; KRMN posted a record Q2 on August 7 with raised guidance; ITA rides a still-accelerating global rearmament cycle; WELL continues its senior-housing NOI growth), so none breached thesis or showed a peak-plus-overweight signal within the quarter. The one action taken was thematic sharpening within the existing cap: swapping Teradyne (a soft-quarter, largely AI-adjacent chip-test name whose robotics exposure is a small subsidiary sliver) for KOID, giving the watchlist its first direct, pure-play channel into the profile's explicitly named robotics wave right as September's $1B+ Figure AI raise signals that wave moving from quiet buildup into an early capital surge.
